2. Opposite Party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the suit against the petitioners and others for a decree of declaration that the waqf estate of which the plaintiff is the mutawalli has got title in the suit land measuring about 1.34 acres fully described in the schedule to the plaint. The petitioners have appeared in the suit and filed a joint written statement denying the plaint case. Then, on 14.02.2002 the petitioners made an application under Order VI Rule 11 of the Code for rejection of the plaint mainly on the ground that the suit as framed was barred by provision of Section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. 1 of 1962), in brief, the Ordinance. On 20.05.2002 the application was heard and rejected by the impugned order on the view that jurisdiction vests in Civil Court only to decide question of title and correctness of the record of rights pre-pared and published in respect of the suit land. 

 5. In the plaint, amongst other, it is averred that Khan Saheb Maulavi Abdul Khaleque created a waqf in the name of Ama Miah Waqf by a registered deed of waqf being No. 1878 dated 10 Falgoon, 1323 BS. Under the terms of the Waqf, property could be acquired out of the fund of the Waqf but transfer of any land of the Waqf was prohibited. In 1917, the Waqf was enrolled being No. 1526 in the office of the Bengal Waqf Commissioner. Out of the fund of the waqf, the suit land was purchased. When the Defendant No. 1 to 4 and 9 to 13 started talking for sale of the suit land, the present mutawalli enquired about the matter and found that the suit land was not recorded in S A record of rights in the name of the waqf. In order to remove the cloud cast by the wrong record, the mutawalli was constrained to institute the suit for a declaration that the waqf has got title in the suit land. 

 6. The issues involved in such suit are whether or not the waqf has got title in the suit land and whether or not the record of rights in respect of the suit land as pre-pared and published is correct. The issues are essentially civil in nature. Under Section 9 of the Code all suits of civil nature will lie in civil courts unless the same is specially barred by specific provision of law. It is now well settled by a long line of authorities that jurisdiction of a civil court cannot readily be read to have stood ousted. 

 8. Firstly, under the. Ordinance the waqf Administrator is given specified powers for the management and administration of the waqfs only. No power of a civil court is given to the Waqf Administrator to decide any civil dispute, namely, question as to title of a property, correctness of a record of rights, validity of a transfer of a waqf property etc. In the case of Syed Masud All and others v Md.
